results.title: AI-Based Models for Predicting Financial Crises and ...
results.content: This article provides a comprehensive analysis of AI-based models for predicting financial crises and recessions, examining their methodologies, real-world applications, performance metrics, and future prospects. Their model achieved significant improvements over traditional methods, with particularly strong performance in identifying banks at risk during the 2008 Financial Crisis. Recent advances in multi-modal learning have enabled the development of sophisticated crisis prediction systems that simultaneously analyze market data, news sentiment, social media, and network relationships to provide holistic risk assessments. Central banks worldwide have begun incorporating AI-based crisis prediction models into their monetary policy frameworks. Central banks use AI models to continuously monitor systemic risk and identify emerging threats to financial stability. These systems process vast amounts of real-time data from financial markets, banking sectors, and economic indicators to provide comprehensive risk assessments. Banks use AI-based crisis prediction models to enhance their credit risk management frameworks. The evidence from implementations by major central banks, financial institutions, and regulatory agencies demonstrates that AI-based crisis prediction models can deliver significant improvements over traditional approaches.

results.title: Financial perceptions and AI infringement risks
results.content: # Financial perceptions and AI infringement risks. Artificial intelligence (AI)-related intellectual property (IP) infringement involves the unauthorized use of copyrighted materials during model training and the creation of content that may violate copyright, trademark, or patent laws. This phenomenon presents critical financial risks for businesses, ranging from reputational harm and erosion of brand equity to potential litigation, regulatory scrutiny, and increased investor uncertainty. To do so, we apply social capital theory to an analysis of 10,447 Chinese social media users' reactions to China's first AI-generated voice infringement lawsuit. Our findings suggest that out-tie social capital (exposure to diverse networks) tends to promote neutral or positive views, while in-tie social capital (strong, close-knit communities) initially encourages favorable attitudes but shifts toward ethical and risk concerns when potential financial damages are perceived. Our study, thus, highlights the interplay between social perception and corporate financial considerations in an era where AI increasingly shapes economic opportunities and liabilities. ## Data availability. results.title: The power of bridging decision scales: Model coupling for ...
results.content: This perspective suggests that coupling existing modeling approaches—exemplified but not limited to IAM, CGE, and ABM—is an increasingly feasible, effective, and useful tool to address emerging climate policy challenges involving multiple actors across different decision scales in nature–society systems. Modeling the mitigation-adaptation nexus will require aligning: i) ABM strengths to represent social interactions among behaviorally diverse actors, technological innovation and diffusion among heterogeneous firms, or climate risk propagation in financial networks; ii) CGE abilities to capture data-driven cross-sector and cross-regional trade-offs and spillovers; and iii) IAM power to consolidate feedback loops between socioeconomic and climate systems. Maintaining these strengths in a coupled modeling system enables the systematic investigation of cross-scale interactions critical to assessing synergies and trade-offs between mitigation and adaptation goals, quantifying transition and physical risks for various economic actors, and supporting more coordinated responses to climate change at local, national, and global scales.
